sides.name: Israel (Southern Command)
sides.note: Strength: 70,000 men and 800 tanks in the Sinai campaign (Dupuy, Elusive Victory pp.240-244, tabulated in DTIC ADA325045 Table A-2); three divisions of ~15,000 men and ~300 tanks each (Herzog via DTIC ADA393361). infantry_line = 70,000 minus tank crews, gunners and support, educated. Half-tracks (ifv_apc) and artillery are educated guesses (Sharon alone massed ~90 guns at Abu Ageila, Wikipedia/Oren). Aircraft: IAF ~250-275 combat aircraft (Oren; Gawrych), nearly all used against Egypt on 5 June: Mirage IIICJ/Super Mystere as fighters, Mystere IV/Ouragan/Vautour/Fouga as strike, educated split. Starts: Tal (Rafah/Khan Yunis), Yoffe (between), Sharon (Nitzana, vs Abu Ageila), southern feint from Eilat/Kuntilla. Tech (derived:tech-anchor, 1967 between 8 and 9): communications 8.5 (radio down to tank level, mission orders); air 8.6 (Mirage III). Ratings: command 0.85 (Tal, Sharon, Yoffe; combined-arms flanking plan); morale 0.85 (perceived existential threat); training 0.75 (reservist army with long annual training). Surprise: Operation Focus destroyed the Egyptian air force on the ground in the first hours. riverCrossing false: the Sinai advance was overland and stopped on the canal, which was not crossed (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War). objective kind capture: Israeli units drove to and stopped along the Suez Canal before the 9 June ceasefire, inside this window (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War).

sides.name: Egypt (Sinai Field Army)
sides.note: Strength: ~100,000 of Egypt's 160,000 troops in the Sinai in seven divisions plus independent brigades, 900-950 tanks, 1,100 APCs, >1,000 guns (Pollack 2004 p.59 via Wikipedia); Dupuy: 100,000 men, 930 tanks (DTIC ADA325045); DTIC ADA393361: ~100,000 soldiers, 1,000 tanks. infantry_line ~70% of the 100,000, educated. Aircraft: 419-420 combat aircraft (Morris, Oren): MiG-21/19/17 as fighters, Su-7, Il-28, Tu-16 as strike (educated split); ~300 destroyed on 5 June. Starts: Rafah/Gaza (7th Inf Div, 20th Palestinian Div), El Arish, Abu Ageila-Umm Katef (2nd Inf Div), Kusseima, Jebel Libni/Bir Hasana (armoured reserve), Shazly Force near Kuntilla/Nakhl, Bir Gifgafa. Tech: T-54/55, IS-3, SU-100, MiG-21 (Soviet early-1960s kit, near Israeli level); fortification 8 = Abu Ageila and Rafah defended localities in depth. Ratings: command 0.25 ('ad hoc': Amer ordered a general withdrawal after Abu Ageila fell on 6 June); morale 0.45; training 0.45 (one third reservists, one third Yemen veterans). prepared true: Egypt had constructed fortified defences in the Sinai, e.g. the heavily fortified Um-Katef area at Abu-Ageila (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War). objective kind hold: Egypt held El Arish and the Sinai defences at the start; Israeli forces took the city on 5-6 June (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six-Day_War).

outcome.note: 5 June 0815 - ceasefire 9 June 0435 on the Sinai front. Israel (Sinai): 275 killed and 61 tanks lost (DTIC ADA393361 citing Herzog); war total 776-983 killed, 4,517 wounded; Sinai wounded share is an educated estimate (~800-1,500). Egypt: 9,800-15,000 killed or missing (El Gamasy; Herzog), 4,338 captured, wounded unknown (educated 2,000-15,000); DTIC ADA393361 gives 12,000 men and 700 tanks lost. Grade C on losses.
